column1: # AGGREGATION -- sum, least and greatest over a finite, settled bag.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# The review's finding I: "`length()` counts but nothing sums: an
# invoice total, a fleet-wide resource budget, a quota roll-up -- all
# inexpressible." A fold over a bag the model already holds is as TOTAL
# as `each` is: no recursion, no user-supplied step, each child visited
# once. That is why these are built-ins rather than a `fold` combinator
# -- a fold takes a function, and this language has none to give it.
# EVERY EXPECTATION HERE WAS OBTAINED BY RUNNING BOTH ENGINES AND
# DIFFING. `canon` rather than `gen`, because half of what these promise
# is the KIND of the answer and a gen row cannot see one.
# THE NAMES ARE `least` AND `greatest`, NOT `min` AND `max`: those two
# are already the constraint atoms for a lower and an upper BOUND, and
# an aggregate over a set is a different thing from a bound on a value.
# WHAT THE ROWS PIN:
#   sum FOLDS WITH add, so the number tower's whole law arrives with it
#   (see arith.tsv): the exact ladder (agg-sum-ladder), R5 contagion
#   (agg-sum-float-contagion), and the refusal to store a result that
#   will not fit (agg-sum-overflow).
#   sum([]) IS 0 and least([]) IS AN ERROR. Addition has an identity, so
#   the empty sum is answerable; comparison has none, and answering with
#   a zero or an infinity would invent a value the data does not
#   contain.
#   COMPARISON IS EXACT, never through binary64: 2^53+1 as a biginteger
#   and 2^53 as an integer have the SAME float image, so a port
#   comparing through doubles would call them equal and return whichever
#   it saw first. agg-least-exact-compare and agg-greatest-exact-compare
#   are that pair.
#   THE WINNER KEEPS ITS OWN KIND (agg-least-keeps-kind): least is one
#   of the elements, not a new value computed from them.
#   ORDER IS each's ORDER -- source order for a list, sorted-key order
#   for a map -- which matters for nothing here except that it is
#   stated, since every operation is commutative.
# THE ERROR ROWS PIN CODES, NOT MESSAGES, and deliberately: where an
# argument is an unresolved reference the two ports render the failing
# call's own canon differently inside the frame (TS `sum(nil)`, Go
# `sum($.a)`). That is pre-existing frame prose -- `upper($.a)` diverges
# the same way and predates this family -- and no row pins it.
agg-sum-list
agg-sum-empty
agg-sum-map
agg-sum-float-contagion
agg-sum-bigdecimal
agg-sum-ladder
agg-sum-pref-member
agg-sum-single
agg-least-list
agg-greatest-list
agg-least-map
agg-greatest-map
agg-least-single
agg-least-keeps-kind
agg-least-pref-member
agg-sum-over-each
# A bag that is not yet resolved residuates and the call is rebuilt.
agg-forward-reference
agg-greatest-exact-compare
agg-least-exact-compare
# The refusals.
agg-least-empty
agg-greatest-empty
agg-sum-not-a-bag
agg-least-not-a-bag
agg-sum-string-member
# A container member reaches the fold's kind check (the signature
# gate judges the BAG argument's shape, not its members).
agg-sum-map-member
agg-least-string-member
agg-sum-overflow
agg-arity
# PROJECTION -- pick(d, k): one element per child of d, being that
# child's k.
# The other half of finding I. Without it the aggregates above cannot
# reach the case that motivated them, because `sum` needs a bag of
# NUMBERS and a model holds a bag of RECORDS:
#   total: sum(pick($.lines, amountCents))
# IT IS NOT `each` WITH A CLEVER TEMPLATE. each(d, t) MEETS each child
# with t, and a meet cannot select: `each($.lines, _.amount)` asks for a
# child that is simultaneously the whole record and one of its fields,
# which is why every spelling of it answers no_path.
# A CHILD MISSING THE KEY IS AN ERROR (pick_key), not a silently shorter
# list -- skipping would make the aggregate over it total a DIFFERENT
# set of records than the one the author named. A list child takes an
# INDEX, spelled as a reference segment is (pick-list-index), and an
# index past the end is the same refusal as a missing key.
pick-list-of-maps
pick-map-of-maps
pick-list-index
pick-empty-bag
pick-then-sum
pick-then-greatest
pick-keeps-kind
pick-nested-value
pick-missing-key
pick-not-a-bag
pick-key-not-a-name
# A FLOAT is not an index either: a list position is an integer, and
# `0.0` is not the spelling a reference segment would use for one.
pick-key-float-index
# ... nor a null, nor a kind: the key names a field, and only a
# string or an integer index can.
pick-key-null
pick-key-kind
pick-scalar-child
pick-index-out-of-range
pick-arity
# PICK AND EACH SHARE ONE ORDER, and it is CODE POINT order -- the
# order canon emits and the one keyorder.ts exists to state. TypeScript
# sorted this one call site with a bare `.sort()`, which is UTF-16 CODE
# UNIT order: an astral key is a surrogate pair beginning D800-DBFF, so
# it sorted BELOW U+E000-U+FFFF and `pick` answered in a different order
# from `each`, from canon, and from Go. `pick` is the order-preserving
# projection a generator turns a bag of records into ordered lines with,
# so that was one model producing two different files (BUGS.md 62).
# The rows are the claim in full: the map's own order, `each`'s and
# `pick`'s all agree, and all three put U+FFF0 before U+1F600. The
# three-key row spans the whole range in one order -- ASCII `a`, then
# BMP U+FFF0, then astral U+1F600 -- which is the ordering a bare
# `.sort()` gets wrong in the middle.
pick-astral-key-order
each-astral-key-order
pick-astral-key-order-three
